title: Synthesize accurate usage events for vector & structured non-chat endpoints
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background:

We occasionally observe discrepancies between tokens/units charged and the golden request payloads for non-chat endpoints (vectorize/embed, rerank endpoints, and structured-output/function-calling flows invoked via non-chat routes). Symptoms reported by customers and internal analytics: unexpected spikes in billed units after retries, double-counting when a function-calling hook triggers multiple downstream tool requests, missing attribution when structured outputs are returned in streaming chunks, and inconsistent rate-limit enforcement for multi-stage requests.

Problem statement:

Our current billing pipeline relies on optimistic per-request accounting emitted from the frontend router and augmented by downstream workers. This model is fragile for multi-stage non-chat flows where a single user request can spawn:
- one or more embedding vector calls (document+query),
- a rerank call that performs internal candidate scoring, and/or
- a function/tool invocation (HTTP/webhook) that itself triggers structured responses and retries.

Because events are emitted from multiple places and some components only emit final summaries while others emit per-chunk/stream events, we see:
- Overcounting: duplicate meter events for the same logical unit when retries or fallbacks occur.
- Undercounting: when streaming chunks are not reconciled into the canonical final usage event.
- Misattribution: cost assigned to the wrong endpoint/model/route (e.g., tool-call charges appearing under the parent requester).
- Incorrect rate limiting: burst limits are bypassed when sub-requests are handled in separate quota contexts.

Goal:

Design and implement a canonical usage-event synthesis layer for non-chat endpoints (embeddings, rerank, structured output, and function-calling flows) that:
1) Emits exactly one canonical usage event per logical user request for billing,
2) Attributes cost to the correct customer/model/route,
3) Correctly handles streaming vs final completion semantics, retries, and partial failures, and
4) Restores correct quota/rate limit behavior across multi-stage request graphs.

Proposed approach:

1) Canonical request id propagation: ensure every incoming non-chat API request is stamped with a deterministic request_id at the edge and propagated to all downstream workers and tool-call contexts. For generated sub-requests (rerank steps, internal vector requests) keep a parent_request_id tag.

2) Event types and lifecycle: define small set of usage event types: request.start, token.delta (streaming chunks), request.complete, request.fail, subrequest.attribution. Only request.complete (or request.fail) will be considered the authoritative event for billing reconciliation; token.delta events will be used for near-real-time dashboards but ignored by the final billing pass unless a final complete never arrives within a bounded window.

3) Deterministic aggregation window: if request.complete does not appear within 30s of the last token.delta, a reconciliation job marks the request as timed_out and attempts to synthesize a complete event based on observed deltas and KV cache usage.

4) Tool-call accounting: when a user-request triggers an external tool call, the tool-call meter must report to billing with parent_request_id and tool_request_id. The synthesis layer will collapse tool-call charges into either the parent request (default) or present them as separate line-items if the caller is explicitly configured to bill separately (tenant-level setting).

5) Quota enforcement: implement a pre-check at edge that reserves quota for the entire logical request graph (best-effort estimate based on prompt sizes + model profile). Downstream quota checks use the reserved token budget and only charge against it. On fallback/hot-reload where a different model variant is used, the reserve is reconciled to the final model's unit cost at request.complete time.

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit tests and integration tests that demonstrate single canonical billing event for: simple embed request, embed+rerank pipeline, rerank with function-call that triggers one external tool, and rerank with partial-tool failure and retry.
- Reduction of duplicate billing events in production traces by >= 90% for affected flows.
- Quota checks prevented >95% of cross-tenant burst bypass cases in staging.
- Audit logs show parent_request_id present for all synthesized billing events in a 48-hour sample.

Implementation plan:

Phase 1 (spike, 1 week):
- Implement deterministic request_id propagation in the edge router and SDKs.
- Add lightweight event schema and start emitting request.start and token.delta for non-chat endpoints.
- Create test harness to simulate multi-stage request graphs.

Phase 2 (core synthesis, 2 weeks):
- Build the synthesis service that listens to stream of events and emits authoritative request.complete events, with de-duplication logic keyed by request_id + parent_request_id.
- Add reconciliation job for timed_out requests.
- Extend current billing pipeline to accept synthesized canonical events.

Phase 3 (tool-call & quota, 2 weeks):
- Wire tool-call attribution into synthesis service and implement tenant-level billing policy flag.
- Implement quota reservation API at edge and downstream quota reconciliation.

Phase 4 (QA & rollout, 1 week):
- Run end-to-end tests in staging, run shadow billing against production, and roll forward gate by usage percentage.

Monitoring and metrics:

- New metrics: canonical_events_emitted, duplicate_events_detected, synthesized_timeouts, quota_reservations_success, quota_bypass_attempts.
- Dashboards: per-route duplicate-rate, per-tenant spend-delta (shadow vs live), percent of events missing parent_request_id.
- Alerts: duplicate_events_detected > 0.5% for 10m, synthesized_timeouts spike > 2x baseline.

Rollout plan:

- Stage: shadow billing in prod for 1 week (no customer impact).
- Canary: 5% of requests routed to synthesis pipeline with actual billing enforcement for internal test tenants.
- Gradual ramp: 5 -> 25 -> 50 -> 100 over 2-3 days with sanity checks at each step.

Documentation and customer communication:

- Update Billing FAQ and Quota docs to explain canonical events and how tool-call billing is attributed.
- Prepare a customer-facing note for tenants who were previously affected, with a link to a CSV export tool to reconcile historical differences.

Risks and mitigations:

- Risk: missed request.complete events for long-running tool calls. Mitigation: extend reconciliation window for configured tenants and ensure token.delta durable storage.
- Risk: increased latency at edge due to quota reservation. Mitigation: best-effort reserve with non-blocking fallback and retryable reconciliation at completion time.

Open questions:

- Should tenants have an opt-out to keep tool-call charges separate by default? (PM decision pending)
- What is the exact SLA for synthesizing timed_out requests for billing (30s vs 120s)?

2026-02-20 - Eng review: decided to treat request.complete as authoritative for billing and keep token.delta for near-real-time dashboards only. See review notes: https://gh.redwood.ai/r/12345
2026-02-24 - Design review: Product asked for tenant opt-out flag for tool-call separation; added to scope for Phase 3.
2026-03-01 - PR opened for synthesis service: platform/pulls/478 - initial de-dup and timed_out reconcilier. Requesting review from billing and infra.
